name: Omega Swarm
product: SmartCiti.X : Trade Craft Academy (powered by AGI Corp)

honesty.scripted: Every software member is a SCRIPTED role already in the Omega Hive or Omega Claw registries; every robot is an AUTHORED simulated robot. No AI model runs behind any of them (models: 0).
honesty.simulation_only: Nothing in this pack sends a command to a real robot or a device. Every routed command is a dry run against the robotics arena worlds, and every robot command passes through safety_gate/ first.
honesty.real_hardware: real hardware needs a named human operator; none is configured. No code in swarm/ sends anything to a robot or a device. The router has no real-hardware path at all, so naming an operator does not open one: a command that names real hardware, a live mode, an operator or a target outside this registry is refused with the sentence above.
honesty.gate: The safety gate decides whether a person may enter a hazardous training station or simulator seat. It is not a real-world safety system. It is not a real-world safety system and no standard is claimed. A simulated robot holds no induction, PPE or permit, so a hazardous seat holds its command; a world the gate has no record for runs as a headless dry run and the audit row says so.
honesty.location: No learner location is stored or sent. Robot and role positions are poses already in the repo (campuses, anchors, restoration sites) or the centre of a parish outline, never a person.
honesty.geopose: Positions are copied from spatial/registry/geopose.json (horizontal only; height and heading are UNKNOWN there and unused here). A pose is a map anchor, not a parcel.
honesty.sim_to_real: A dry run is a SCHEMATIC simulation of an AUTHORED task. Its numbers say nothing about how a physical robot would behave.
honesty.standards: Geohash is used as a public-domain cell scheme; this pack makes no conformance claim to any robotics or fleet-management standard.

cell_scheme.name: geohash
cell_scheme.why: Geohash is a public-domain, prefix-addressed grid, so a coarser cell string names every cell below it and a cell set can be written by hand. Precision 5 is a cell about 4.9 km by 4.9 km at the equator (narrower in longitude further north): small enough that a campus and its neighbours are different cells, large enough that a hive has a handful of cells, not thousands. Each campus also owns the ring of cells around its own cell, so a fence drawn around a campus finds its hive even where no anchor is recorded.

cluster_rule.name: single-linkage
cluster_rule.why: Campuses within 100 km of each other (a metro area) share one hive; a campus further than that from every other has its own. Measured with the haversine distance between the campus GeoPose positions.

parish_rule.why: A Hive parish guide stands at the centre of its parish outline (the middle of the outline's bounding box, DERIVED). The parish joins the nearest hive, and the build fails if that hive's home campus is more than this far away.

robot_placement_rule: A simulated robot stands at one pose of its own campus (the campus, its anchors and its restoration sites), chosen by sha256('<robot id>:place') mod the number of eligible poses; a survey ROV prefers a restoration site when its campus has one. A placement is a position in a schematic simulation, not a statement that any robot exists there.

dry_run.epoch_note: A fixed instant (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) handed to the safety gate as 'now' so a dry run reads no clock and gives the same answer every time.

real_hardware.refusal: real hardware needs a named human operator; none is configured
real_hardware.rule: No code in swarm/ sends anything to a robot or a device. The router has no real-hardware path at all, so naming an operator does not open one: a command that names real hardware, a live mode, an operator or a target outside this registry is refused with the sentence above.

optimise.task_rule: One training-task slot per cell that holds a campus, anchor or restoration-site pose. Its kind is task_kinds[sha256('<cell>:task')[:8] mod 4]. A robot can only take a task whose capability names its own embodiment, and only within max_km of the cell centre.

unposed.why: no GeoPose: the registry pins no single coordinate for this bay-wide program (pin: false, lat/lng null), and this build invents none

robot.gate-drive.summary: Simulated rover runs the gate-drive arena task in dry-run. The task is the forklift-run bay-yard lane, so the safety gate holds it.
robot.gate-drive.gate_note: the arena world is the bay-yard lane of the forklift-run seat; the gate holds every one of that seat's hall records

robot.litter-pickup.summary: Simulated rover runs the litter-pickup arena task in dry-run.
robot.litter-pickup.gate_note: the gate index (stations and simulator seats) holds no record for this headless arena world, so it answers unknown-target

robot.litter-sort.summary: Simulated arm runs the litter-sort arena task in dry-run.
robot.litter-sort.gate_note: the gate index (stations and simulator seats) holds no record for this headless arena world, so it answers unknown-target

robot.rov-survey.summary: Simulated ROV runs the monitoring-survey arena task in dry-run.
robot.rov-survey.gate_note: the gate index (stations and simulator seats) holds no record for this headless arena world, so it answers unknown-target

software.advise-visitor.summary: The hive's Orientation guide offers its quoted greeting line.

greeting.value: First time in this hall? Ask me what it is and where to start.

software.audit-dataset.summary: The hive's Data Steward reports the robot-learning dataset's own audit numbers.

software.schedule-tournament.summary: The hive's Scheduler reports the tournament queue it builds.
